task.title: Acknowledged warning hysteresis
task.specification: config={low:integer,high:integer,dwell:positive integer},low<high. Initially lastTime=-1,normal enabled=true, invisible, no critical ID. observe={type:'observe',t:nonnegative integer,level:integer,critical:boolean,id:ID}. Observations with t<=lastTime are ignored; every newer observation advances lastTime. An unacknowledged critical observation immediately shows kind='critical' with its ID and resets normal counters, even when normal mode is disabled; it replaces any previous critical ID. An acknowledged critical ID is ignored apart from lastTime. While critical is visible, normal observations do not change it. Otherwise, when enabled, dwell consecutive newer normal observations level>=high turn an invisible warning on; dwell consecutive level<=low turn a visible normal warning off. Any other newer normal value resets that counter. High and low equality count. ack={type:'ack',id} permanently records the ID; if it matches visible critical, hide it and reset counters. mode={type:'mode',enabled:boolean} resets normal counters, and hides a normal warning only when disabled; it never hides a critical warning. Output {visible:boolean,kind:'normal'|'critical'|null,id:ID|null}, id is nonnull only for visible critical. No timer or future observations are available. Return one output per event. State is opaque JSON, initially null. Output objects have exactly the documented keys; object key order is irrelevant, array order is significant. IDs are nonempty ASCII strings. Values are JSON scalars unless stated otherwise. Numeric values and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers; integral JSON notations such as 1 and 1.0 denote the same number, while booleans are distinct. Strings contain Unicode scalar values without unpaired surrogates. Inputs have at most 48 events and eight simultaneous identities. Ordinary instances vary values; boundary instances emphasize empty/disabled/equality/no-op states; adversarial instances reorder callbacks and interleave edits; shift instances use longer traces/more identities within the same rules. These tasks test controller state/effects only, not visual quality, browser integration or screen-reader usability.

matchedCard.label: Lighthouse sector signals
matchedCard.relation: A navigational source can provide a general identifying signal and a separate directional indication for a particular hazard. What a sector indication signifies depends on the observer's position and its relationship to the marked region.
assumptions: The source and the meaning of its sector can be identified.
The observer has sufficient visibility and positional context to interpret the indication.
matchedCard.boundary: A sector signal describes only its designated region. An ordinary indication does not certify that every nearby route is hazard-free, and poor visibility can limit interpretation.
matchedCard.source_fact: Trinity House describes Start Point's white navigational flashes and a separate red sector marking the shallow Skerries Bank, alongside a low-visibility hazard warning signal.

sources.title: Trinity House completes re-engineering of Start Point Lighthouse

shuffledCard.label: Cartographic generalization
shuffledCard.relation: At a smaller representation scale, selection, simplification, and combination can preserve legibility while omitting detail. The resulting representation depends on scale and purpose; omission from that representation does not establish absence from the represented world.
assumptions: The representation has a specified scale and communicative purpose.
A more detailed source contains distinctions from which the representation is derived.
shuffledCard.boundary: Simplification can remove a distinction important for another purpose. A reduced representation cannot recover information that it does not encode.
shuffledCard.source_fact: USGS describes cartographic generalization as selecting and reducing detail to produce representations appropriate to scale.

initial.explanation: Use a finite controller state: newest observation time, mode, warning kind/ID, hysteresis counters, and acknowledged IDs. Newer observations alone advance time; critical observations take priority unless acknowledged. Normal hysteresis operates only while enabled and no critical warning is visible.
initial.mapping: config thresholds map to up/down consecutive-normal counters; state stores lastTime, enabled, visible kind/id, counters, and acknowledged IDs; event types transition these variables; output projects visibility, kind, and critical ID.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the published validity constraints. IDs are compared by exact string equality. Initial state is null and all supplied events are processed synchronously in order.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!applies(input)||!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;var s=null;for(var i=0;i<output.length;i++){var r=solve({config:input.config,state:s,event:input.events[i]});s=r.state;var a=r.output,b=output[i];if(!b||b.visible!==a.visible||b.kind!==a.kind||b.id!==a.id)return false}return true}

final.explanation: Maintains the newest observation time, enabled mode, visible warning, hysteresis counters, and acknowledged critical IDs. Observations only affect behavior when newer than the recorded time. Unacknowledged critical observations take priority; normal observations are ignored while critical is visible. Mode changes reset counters, and acknowledgements hide only a matching critical warning.

initial.explanation: Use timestamp ordering, acknowledgement identity, critical precedence, mode state, and directional hysteresis counters. The optional lighthouse analogy is not needed because this is a deterministic event controller.
initial.mapping: lastTime maps observation ordering; ack maps permanently acknowledged IDs; criticalId maps the currently visible critical identity; enabled maps mode; dir/count map consecutive high or low normal observations; kind/visible map rendered warning state.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated schema and limits. Configuration remains valid for the trace. State is returned unchanged in meaning but may use a compact JSON object.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;let c=input.config,s={t:-1,e:true,d:0,n:0,k:null,id:null,a:[]};function o(){return{visible:s.k!==null,kind:s.k,id:s.k==='critical'?s.id:null}}for(let i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){let x=input.events[i];if(x.type==='ack'){if(s.a.indexOf(x.id)<0)s.a.push(x.id);if(s.k==='critical'&&s.id===x.id){s.k=null;s.id=null;s.d=0;s.n=0}}else if(x.type==='mode'){s.e=x.enabled;s.d=0;s.n=0;if(!s.e&&s.k==='normal')s.k=null}else if(x.type==='observe'&&x.t>s.t){s.t=x.t;if(x.critical&&s.a.indexOf(x.id)<0){s.k='critical';s.id=x.id;s.d=0;s.n=0}else if(!x.critical&&s.k!=='critical'&&s.e){let q=x.level>=c.high?1:x.level<=c.low?-1:0;if(q===0||q!==s.d){s.d=q;s.n=q?1:0}else s.n++;if(s.n>=c.dwell){if(q===1)s.k='normal';else if(q===-1)s.k=null;s.n=0}}}let z=o(),y=output[i];if(!y||y.visible!==z.visible||y.kind!==z.kind||y.id!==z.id)return false}return true}

final.explanation: Maintains last-observation time, permanent acknowledgements, mode, critical identity, and directional hysteresis counters. Newer critical observations take precedence unless acknowledged; critical visibility blocks normal processing. Mode changes reset counters and disabling hides only normal warnings. Each event returns the exact documented output shape.

initial.explanation: Use a finite controller state: last observation time, acknowledged IDs, mode, normal hysteresis counters, and current warning. Critical observations take precedence unless their ID was acknowledged.
initial.mapping: config.low/high/dwell map to hysteresis thresholds and persistence. State maps to lastTime, acknowledgements, enabled mode, counters, and visible warning. Events map to ordered transitions; output is the resulting warning projection.
initial.assumptions: The host supplies the same config on each call and passes returned JSON state unchanged. Event types are valid under the specification. IDs are compared by exact string equality.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;for(const x of output){if(!x||typeof x!=="object"||typeof x.visible!=="boolean"||!(x.kind===null||x.kind==="normal"||x.kind==="critical"))return false;if(x.visible!==(x.kind!==null))return false;if(x.kind==="critical"&&typeof x.id!=="string")return false;if(x.kind!=="critical"&&x.id!==null)return false}return true}

final.explanation: Maintains lastTime, permanent acknowledgements, mode, hysteresis counters, and the current warning. Newer critical observations take precedence unless acknowledged; critical visibility blocks normal processing. Mode changes reset counters, and disabling hides only normal warnings. Outputs are projected with exactly the required fields.
